In 1919, on the set of the silent film *Soldiers of Fortune* , a script existed mostly as a continuity outline that a director, camera operator, and crew improvised around. There was no dialogue to format, because there was no recorded dialogue at all. The strict industry screenplay, with its scene headings, centered character names, and page-per-minute pacing, only hardened into a standard once sound arrived a decade later.


In 2026, you can type "a two-minute YouTube script about morning routines" or "a feature screenplay about a heist gone wrong" and get a draft back in seconds. The catch is that "script generator" now means two different jobs. A produced screenplay follows a rigid format built for a crew to read at a glance. A YouTube or ad script is closer to plain, spoken prose. Pick a tool built for one when you need the other, and the output looks wrong from the first page.


> **TL;DR:** We sorted **15 AI script generators by what they actually format** : industry screenplays (Squibler, Arc Studio, WriterDuet, Celtx, Final Draft, Trelby), video and social scripts (Restream, Teleprompter.com, Subscribr, Descript, Jasper), and free general assistants (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT). Free tiers, export formats, and rights verified September 24, 2026. Outline the story first with[free script generators](https://www.taskade.com/generate/content/movie-script) .


---

Arc Studio and WriterDuet format what you write and export Fountain and Final Draft files. For a free video script with no sign-up, Restream is fastest. ## What Is an AI Script Generator?


**An AI script generator is any tool that turns a written prompt into a script, but "script" splits into two formats that rarely overlap.** An industry screenplay uses a rigid layout built for a crew: scene headings, action lines, and centered, capitalized character names, all timed to roughly a page per minute of screen time. A video script for YouTube, TikTok, a podcast, or an ad has no such standard. It is closer to a spoken essay, written to be read aloud or displayed on a teleprompter.


A third category sits underneath both: the outline and beat sheet that should exist before either kind of script gets written. Most comparisons skip this stage entirely and jump straight to prose generation.

```text
A first draft in any format           Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT              Plain text or markdown
The outline before any of the above   Taskade generators                   Logline, beat sheet, outline


```


---


## What a Script Actually Is, Before AI Writes One


**A script, of any kind, is a plan for what happens in order: who does what, in what setting, saying what.** That is true whether the output is a two-hour screenplay or a ninety-second TikTok script. The part that makes a script work is decided before the prose gets written: the logline, the beat sheet, and the scene list. Skip that and a generator writes the average of every script it has seen, which is the flat, familiar feeling readers describe as "obviously AI."


A typewritten screenplay page prop from The Shining, photographed at a Stanley Kubrick exhibit. The industry screenplay format existed decades before any of it was AI-generated. Photo: William Beutler / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY 2.0.


Most tools in this list start at step five. Arc Studio and Final Draft give you a beat board to arrange cards on, but none of them write the beat sheet for you, which is the gap the closing section of this article covers.


The length of the draft follows two rules of thumb, one for each format:


```text
SCRIPT LENGTH CARD                        (verified 2026-09-24)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SCREENPLAY  about 1 page per minute of screen time
a 90-minute feature  ≈  90 pages
a 22-minute episode  ≈  22 pages  VIDEO / VOICEOVER  spoken words, per Teleprompter.com presets  30 seconds  →    75-80 words  1 minute    →  150-160 words  3 minutes   →  450-480 words  5 minutes   →  750-800 words  10 minutes  → 1,500-1,600 words  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  Ask a generator for "a 3-minute script" and check the word count.
```

Vendor terms decide who owns the output. Two outside rules decide what that ownership is worth, and most script-tool roundups skip both:

## Screenplay and Film/TV Format Tools


These tools format an industry-standard screenplay. Squibler adds AI drafting on top of the format. Arc Studio sells AI table reads and research as credit add-ons. The other four format and plan the script you write, with no generation feature.


### 1.[Squibler](https://www.squibler.io/) : Best for AI-Drafted Screenplays


[Squibler](https://www.squibler.io/) combines an AI writing assistant with a dedicated screenplay mode that formats dialogue, action lines, scene headings, and transitions to the standard the industry expects. A separate script generator page drafts movie scripts, TV pilots, stage plays, and short video scripts with no account.


Squibler AI Script Writer page, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** AI-assisted drafting inside a proper screenplay mode; import from Microsoft Word, Final Draft, and Google Docs; a combined book-and-script writing environment.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** 1,000 AI credits a month, forever, with no time limit on the free tier itself. Heavy AI use outgrows the credit allowance quickly.


**Pros:**


- The only screenplay editor here that both drafts scenes and formats them as a real screenplay
- Squibler's terms of service grant users full ownership of what they create, including on the free plan
- Genuinely free, ongoing access to the writing environment, not just a trial


**Cons:**


- 1,000 monthly credits run out fast if you rely on AI for full scenes
- Export to PDF and DOCX is reserved for paid tiers


**Pricing:** Plus $29.99/month, or $15.83/month billed annually ($189.96/year). Pro $89.99/month, or $49.17/month billed annually ($588/year).


**Bottom line:** the best starting point if you want AI to draft scenes inside real screenplay formatting.


### 2.[Arc Studio](https://www.arcstudiopro.com/) : Best Free Screenwriting App With Real Formatting


[Arc Studio](https://www.arcstudiopro.com/) is a modern screenwriting editor built around outlining and a visual plot board, alongside standard formatting. It bills annually only, which keeps its entry price well under most monthly subscriptions in this category.


Arc Studio homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** automatic screenplay formatting; a plot board for outlining before you write; revision tracking and version history; Fountain and Final Draft export; AI table reads, character images, and a research assistant, paid for with separate credits.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** two scripts, with a watermark on PDF exports, plus a 7-day Pro trial. No credit card required to sign up.


**Pros:**


- No payment info needed to start, and the free plan is genuinely usable, not a countdown trial
- Fountain and Final Draft export means your work is never locked into Arc Studio alone
- Outlining and plot-board tools built in, not bolted on


**Cons:**


- The free plan caps you at two scripts and stamps a watermark on exports
- No monthly billing option; you commit to a year at a time


**Pricing:** Essentials $69/year. Pro $99/year, with $70 off Pro for students with a .edu address. AI add-on credits cost extra.


**Bottom line:** the best free way to try real screenwriting software before you commit to a year.


### 3.[WriterDuet](https://www.writerduet.com/) : Best for a Free Plan With No Watermark


[WriterDuet](https://www.writerduet.com/) is built around real-time collaborative writing, and unusually for this category, its free plan carries no watermark and no time limit.


WriterDuet homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** industry-standard formatting; real-time co-writing (as a guest on a paid user's project when both of you are free); cloud backups to Google Drive and Dropbox; import and export of Final Draft, Fountain, and PDF files.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** 3 projects, one document each, with read-only collaborators and no watermark on exports.


**Pros:**


- No watermark on the free plan, unusual in this category
- Export formats match the industry standard on every tier, including free
- Real-time collaboration is available as a guest even on the free plan


**Cons:**


- Two free-plan users cannot co-write together as hosts; one side needs a paid plan
- No AI drafting; WriterDuet formats and organizes what you write


**Pricing:** Plus $9.99/month or $89.88/year. Pro $11.99/month or $107.88/year. Premium $13.99/month or $125.88/year.


**Bottom line:** the cleanest free screenwriting environment if collaboration matters more than AI drafting.


### 4.[Celtx](https://www.celtx.com/) : Best for Planning Past the Script Into Production


[Celtx](https://www.celtx.com/) extends past the script itself into pre-production: shot lists, storyboards, and scheduling sit in the same product as the screenplay editor, aimed at teams shooting what they write.


**Key features:** script editor with industry formatting; storyboard and shot-list tools; scheduling and call-sheet features for a shoot; team plans for a full crew.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** a permanent free plan limited to 1 project, separate from a 7-day free trial of the paid Writer and Writer Pro tiers. After the trial, the account reverts to the free tier rather than losing access.


**Pros:**


- The only tool here that plans the shoot, not just the script
- A genuine free tier exists after the trial ends, not just a locked-out account
- Education and student pricing for classroom use


**Cons:**


- The pricing page lists plans but no prices, so you compare costs only after you sign up
- No AI script drafting; Celtx formats and plans, it does not generate


**Pricing:** Writer, Writer Pro, and Team (3 to 15 members) plans, with prices shown after sign-up; Education and Student plans through sales.


**Bottom line:** the right pick when the script is step one of an actual shoot, not the whole project.


### 5.[Final Draft](https://www.finaldraft.com/) : Best for the Format the Industry Already Expects


[Final Draft](https://www.finaldraft.com/) is the screenwriting software most film and television productions still expect by default, and its FDX file format is the one every competing tool in this list exports to for compatibility. Final Draft 13 adds writing-goal tracking, a redesigned Navigator, and Structure Lines for outlining, but it has no AI text generation.


Final Draft 13 product page, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** automatic industry-standard formatting; Beat Board and Outline Editor for structure; production reports; Final Draft Cloud for browser and mobile access alongside the desktop app.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** **none.** A 5-day free trial is available on the Suite subscription.


**Pros:**


- The format readers, agents, and productions expect by default
- Structure and planning tools (Beat Board, Outline Editor) built for the writing process, not just formatting
- Final Draft Cloud keeps a script accessible across desktop, tablet, and browser


**Cons:**


- No free plan and no AI drafting of any kind
- The one-time license lists at $249.99, the highest up-front cost among the screenplay editors here


**Pricing:** Final Draft Suite at $99.99/year or $16.99/month, or a one-time Final Draft 13 license listed at $249.99 and on sale for $199.99 on September 24, 2026.


**Bottom line:** the safe choice when the format itself has to be beyond question.


### 6.[Trelby](https://trelby.org/) : Best Completely Free, Open-Source Screenwriting App


[Trelby](https://trelby.org/) is free, open-source software with no paid tier at all, and unusually broad format support: it imports Final Draft, Celtx, Fountain, Adobe Story, and Fade In files, and exports to PDF, formatted text, HTML, RTF, Final Draft, and Fountain.


**Key features:** industry-standard formatting; a built-in, configurable PDF generator; identical output on Windows, macOS, and Linux (v2.4); the widest import/export format list in this comparison.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** everything, forever, with no account, no watermark, and no paid tier to upgrade to.


**Pros:**


- Genuinely free forever, not a free tier inside a paid product
- Open source, so the software outlives any company's decisions
- The broadest file-format compatibility here, in both directions


**Cons:**


- No AI drafting whatsoever
- The desktop interface looks dated next to newer cloud editors, and its feature list names no real-time co-writing


**Pricing:** free, permanently.


**Bottom line:** the only tool on this list with nothing to upgrade to, and nothing to lose if the company disappears.

## Video, YouTube & Social Script Generators


These tools write plain-text scripts for a camera or a microphone, not an industry screenplay.


### 7.[Restream](https://restream.io/tools/ai-youtube-script-generator) : Best Completely Free Script Generator, No Sign-Up


[Restream](https://restream.io/tools/ai-youtube-script-generator) 's YouTube script generator asks for a topic, audience, and tone, and returns a usable draft with no account required. Restream's main product streams live video to several platforms at once, and the script generator is one of the free tools on its site, useful for planning what you say on that stream or in a recorded video.


Restream AI YouTube Script Generator, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** topic-to-script generation; five tone presets (Professional, Friendly, Confident, Funny, Simple); no sign-up, no credit card, no published cap.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** unlimited script generation, free, with your session data deleted after your visit rather than stored.


**Pros:**


- Genuinely free with zero friction: no account, no card, no limit found
- Fast enough for a same-day draft
- No data retained after your session


**Cons:**


- Scripts are generic compared to purpose-built YouTube tools, with no channel-specific SEO or retention data
- No integration with titles, tags, or thumbnails


**Pricing:** free.


**Bottom line:** the fastest zero-commitment way to get a video script draft today.


### 8.[Teleprompter.com](https://www.teleprompter.com/tools/script-generator) : Best Free Script Generator Built for Reading on Camera


[Teleprompter.com](https://www.teleprompter.com/tools/script-generator) 's script generator produces video scripts for YouTube, social platforms, presentations, and product demos, timed by target length, then opens directly in the site's own teleprompter tool.


Teleprompter.com script generator, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** six length presets from 30 seconds (75-80 words) to 10 minutes (1,500-1,600 words); natural pause points written into the script for on-camera delivery; a direct "open in teleprompter" handoff; copy and download options.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** free and unlimited, with "No Sign Up" in the page title. The site's own teleprompter app, which the script opens into, has its own sign-in.


**Pros:**


- Scripts are written for spoken delivery, with pacing built in
- Direct handoff into a teleprompter, useful if you actually plan to film
- Covers more than YouTube: presentations and product demos too


**Cons:**


- Tone and structure controls are thinner than in a dedicated YouTube tool
- No screenplay or long-form support


**Pricing:** not published beyond the free tool.


**Bottom line:** the best free option when the script's final destination is a camera, not a page.


### 9.[Subscribr](https://subscribr.ai/) : Best for YouTube-Specific Hooks and Retention Data


[Subscribr](https://subscribr.ai/) is built specifically for YouTube scriptwriting, using competitor and trending-content analysis to shape a script's hook and pacing, rather than generating generic prose. Its paid plans now also generate finished video and thumbnails from the script.


**Key features:** YouTube-specific script generation; competitor and trend research; thumbnail generation; video generation priced per minute of finished video.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** a permanent free plan with 1 channel, 3 idea batches a month, and 10 research searches a month, with no card. It includes no script credits, so AI scripts start on Growth.


**Pros:**


- Purpose-built for YouTube retention, not a repurposed general writing tool
- Competitor research is a genuine differentiator versus the free generic tools
- The free plan lets you test the idea and research side before you pay


**Cons:**


- The cheapest plan with AI script credits costs $99 a month, the highest monthly entry price in this list
- Older roundups still quote a $7 trial and a $299 yearly plan that the pricing page no longer shows


**Pricing:** Growth $99/month (60 script credits), Pro $249/month (180), Max $499/month (300), with two months free on annual billing.


**Bottom line:** worth the price only when a channel's growth data matters more than a free draft.


### 10.[Descript](https://www.descript.com/) : Best for Turning a Script Into an Edited Video


[Descript](https://www.descript.com/) is a video and podcast editor whose text-based editing treats a transcript as the timeline, and its AI co-editor, Underlord, can brainstorm, rewrite, or draft a script or outline directly inside that same document.


Descript homepage, captured March 2026.


**Key features:** text-based video and audio editing; Underlord AI for script and outline drafting; transcription; screen recording.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** 60 minutes of media a month, 100 one-time AI credits, 720p export, no credit card required.


**Pros:**


- The script and the edit live in the same tool, so revising the text revises the video
- A genuine, card-free free plan, not just a trial
- Transcription and text-based editing remove a whole manual step for talking-head content


**Cons:**


- 60 minutes a month is tight for anything beyond occasional use
- AI credits on the free plan are one-time, not monthly, so heavy Underlord use needs a paid tier


**Pricing:** Hobbyist $16/month billed annually or $24 monthly, Creator $24/month billed annually or $35 monthly, Business $50/month billed annually or $65 monthly.


**Bottom line:** the right tool when the script is inseparable from the video you are about to cut.


### 11.[Jasper](https://www.jasper.ai/) : Best for On-Brand Marketing Scripts at Scale


[Jasper](https://www.jasper.ai/) offers a dedicated Video Script AI Agent that keeps scripts aligned with a brand's voice and knowledge base, aimed at marketing teams producing many scripts rather than a single creator producing one.


**Key features:** a Video Script AI Agent for ads, demos, and promotional video; brand-voice grounding through Jasper IQ; workflows that scale one script into a full episode library.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** **no permanent free plan.** A 7-day trial of the Pro plan is available with no credit card required to start.


**Pros:**


- Jasper's terms of service grant customers full ownership and commercial rights to generated output
- Built for consistency across many scripts, not just one
- No card required for the trial itself


**Cons:**


- The cheapest ongoing plan, Pro, costs $59 a month billed annually
- Overkill for a single creator who needs one script, not a marketing team's pipeline


**Pricing:** Pro $59/month billed annually, or $69/month billed monthly.


**Bottom line:** the right tool for a team producing scripts at volume, not a solo creator's first draft.


---


## Free General AI Assistants That Can Write a Script


General AI assistants draft a workable first pass of almost any script on their free plans, though none of them format an industry screenplay.


### 12.[Claude](https://claude.ai/) : Best Free Assistant for Drafting and Revising a Script in Chat


[Claude](https://claude.ai/) drafts dialogue, scenes, and full video scripts directly in chat, and its Artifacts feature can hold a longer script as an editable document you revise across a conversation. Code execution and file creation must be switched on in Settings for Artifacts to work.


**Key features:** conversational script drafting and revision; Artifacts for holding a full script as a living document; memory across conversations on every plan, including free.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** available on the Free plan, alongside web search and adaptive thinking. Public sharing of an Artifact is available on Free, Pro, and Max.


**Pros:**


- Free plan access to the same drafting and revision quality as paid tiers, with lower usage limits
- Artifacts keep a long script as one editable document instead of scattered chat replies
- Strong at matching tone and voice across a long back-and-forth revision


**Cons:**


- No screenplay-specific formatting; output is plain text you would still reformat for Final Draft
- Usage limits on the free plan can interrupt a long drafting session


**Pricing:** free, with paid Claude plans for higher limits.


**Bottom line:** the strongest free option for iterating on dialogue and structure through conversation.


### 13.[Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) : Best Free Option on Google's Stack


[Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) 's Canvas feature drafts and edits documents, including scripts, directly in a live preview, and Canvas is included on Gemini's free plan with no separate unlock required.


**Key features:** live document editing in Canvas; version history within a Canvas session; full Google Workspace integration for moving a script into Docs.


**Free plan (verified Sep 24, 2026):** Canvas is included on the free plan; overall usage is compute-based and resets on a rolling window rather than a hard daily cap.


**Pros:**


- Canvas is a genuine free-plan feature, not a paid unlock
- Google Workspace integration makes it easy to hand a script to a collaborator in Docs
- A low-cost upgrade path: Google AI Plus costs $4.99/month if you outgrow free


**Cons:**


- Same lack of screenplay formatting as every general assistant here
- No published hard cap makes it harder to plan a heavy drafting session in advance


**Pricing:** free; Google AI Plus $4.99/month and Google AI Pro $19.99/month for more usage.


**Bottom line:** a strong free alternative to Claude, especially inside the Google ecosystem.

## Why Screenplay Software Still Skips AI Generation


**The screenplay tools with the most trusted formatting, Final Draft, Arc Studio, WriterDuet, and Trelby, write no scenes for you, and that is a choice, not an oversight.** Squibler is the exception: a general writing app with a screenplay mode, not a screenwriting tool built AI-first. Arc Studio's AI reads your script aloud and answers research questions, but leaves the writing to you.


A screenplay's value is structural: the three-act arc, a want colliding with a need, dialogue that reveals character through what is left unsaid. A model trained on millions of scripts produces the average of that structure, which reads as competent and forgettable at once. The video-script side made the opposite bet. A fifteen-second hook or a two-minute demo has far less structure to average away, which is why Restream, Subscribr, and Jasper lead with generation.

## AI Script Generator FAQ


What is the best AI script generator in 2026?


It depends on the script: Squibler for an AI-drafted screenplay, Arc Studio, WriterDuet, or Final Draft for formatting and export, Restream or Teleprompter.com for a free YouTube script, and Taskade's free[script outline](https://www.taskade.com/generate/content-creators/script-outline) generator for the plan that comes first.


What is the best free AI movie script generator?


Squibler's AI script generator page works without an account, and its free plan adds 1,000 AI credits a month for the full screenplay editor. Taskade's free[movie script generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/content/movie-script) drafts a scene-by-scene plan and first pass you can edit with a team, and the[screenplay outline generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/outline/screenplay-outline) builds the act structure first. Trelby, a free open-source editor, then formats the result and exports Fountain and Final Draft files.


Is there a free AI script generator with no sign-up?


Yes. On September 24, 2026, Restream, Teleprompter.com, and Squibler all stated on their script generator pages that no account is needed. Trelby needs no account either, but it formats and writes no AI drafts.


Can AI write a full movie script?


AI can produce a full first draft in minutes, with scene headings, action lines, and dialogue. It does less well at the structure: a three-act arc, goals that pay off, and dialogue that sounds like one person. Give the model a specific character voice, a concrete want, and a constraint, then revise against a real beat sheet.


What is the best AI screenplay formatter?


Arc Studio, WriterDuet, Final Draft, and Trelby format a screenplay automatically as you type, with scene headings, action lines, and centered character names. To convert text you already have, save it as Fountain, a free plain-text screenplay format that all four can import. Taskade's free[screenplay format generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/publishing/screenplay-format) turns a scene description into screenplay layout as a first pass.


What is the best AI YouTube script generator?


Restream and Teleprompter.com are free with no account, Subscribr's $99-a-month Growth plan adds channel and competitor data, and Descript keeps the script and the edit in one document. Taskade's[video script generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/content/video-script) and[video script prompt](https://www.taskade.com/prompts/content/video-script-prompt) are free starting points.


What is the best AI voiceover script generator?


A voiceover script runs about 150 to 160 spoken words a minute, per Teleprompter.com's length presets. Teleprompter.com and Restream draft one free, Descript syncs the script to the audio, and Taskade's free[voiceover script generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/content-creators/voiceover-script) and[voice-over script writer agent](https://www.taskade.com/agents/video-production/voice-over-script-writer) draft narration you can edit with a team before recording.


Can AI write a TV show script?


Yes, as a first pass, and Squibler's generator lists TV pilots among its formats. A series also needs a show bible that keeps characters consistent, where a shared outline and an AI agent with project memory help. Under the 2023 WGA contract, AI-generated material is not literary or source material.


Which AI script generators export to Fountain or Final Draft format?


Arc Studio, WriterDuet, and Trelby all import and export Fountain and Final Draft files, and WriterDuet does so on its free plan. Final Draft's own FDX format is the file the others target. Squibler exports PDF and DOCX on paid plans.


Can I copyright or sell a script written with AI?


You can usually sell it, but copyright covers only the human part. The US Copyright Office stated in January 2025 that prompts alone do not make you the author of AI output. Your own writing, edits, and creative arrangement stay protectable. Squibler's and Jasper's terms grant you ownership of output.


Is ChatGPT good for writing scripts?


ChatGPT can draft a workable first pass of a video script, a scene, a stage play, or dialogue. OpenAI removed Canvas from its GPT-5.5 models on May 28, 2026, and replaced it with writing blocks inside chat on every plan, including free. ChatGPT does not produce industry screenplay formatting, so a produced screenplay still needs a dedicated editor such as Arc Studio or Final Draft.


Does Taskade write scripts?


Taskade is not a screenwriting editor and does not compete with Final Draft or Arc Studio on formatting.
